CAUSE: `_on_task_done()` treats a normally completed per-turn listener as a crash whenever the session happens to be RUNNING when its done callback executes. That status can belong to the *next* turn, not the turn whose listener just ended.

In `TurnManager.handle_turn_end()` (`app/session_turns.py`), `finish_turn_status()` sets the session IDLE, then `after_turn_idle_actions()` claims queued mailbox messages and schedules their delivery. In `app/session.py`, delivery sets the session RUNNING before awaiting backend setup and send. If that happens before the old listener’s done callback runs, `_on_task_done()` sees RUNNING and calls `_finish_failed_running_turn("listen task exited unexpectedly while RUNNING")`. That logs the false error and invokes `report_abnormal_end()`, producing the automatic failure report. The next log row can then show the still-live worker starting another turn.

This fits both excerpts: one shows a failed `rate_limit` turn followed by mailbox continuation; the other shows a normal `turn ended` followed by mailbox continuation. Quota exhaustion can precede the race, but it does not explain the false listener verdict.

I did not reproduce the exact journal sequence from this snapshot. The existing `tests/test_listen_task_done_648.py` checks stale-task identity, but not the window where the next turn is RUNNING before its listener replaces the old task. I recommend associating each listener with the turn generation it serves and ignoring completion callbacks once that generation has advanced; add a regression test for mailbox delivery entering RUNNING before the prior callback runs.
